cards.explanation: The answer is False. The speaker says, "Though I have fallen, I will arise…" (Micah 7:8). The enemy is told not to gloat, because the fall isn't the last word. I think that's a pretty bold thing to say to an enemy, friends.

The answer is light. The speaker says, "though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light." (Micah 7:8). Darkness is the hard part of the sentence, and light is where it lands. I know a little about sitting in the dark, friends, and a line like that hits me right in the apron.

The answer is until the LORD argues the case. The speaker says the rage must be endured "…until He argues my case and executes justice for me." (Micah 7:9). The speaker isn't running the case alone, friends. The LORD takes it up Himself, and I think that's a comfort.

The answer is shame. The enemy "…will see and will be covered with shame…" (Micah 7:10). She's the one who asked, "Where is the LORD your God?" Then she gets to watch what happens, and I think that question is going to feel a lot smaller to her then, friends.

The answer is rebuilding. The message says, "The day for rebuilding your walls will come…" (Micah 7:11). Walls going up and borders growing is a picture of things getting better. I've always liked a day where the work is building instead of cleaning up, friends.

The answer is because of what its people did. The earth becomes desolate "…because of its inhabitants, as the fruit of their deeds." (Micah 7:13). That's a heavy line, friends, so I'll just say it plainly. The text ties the desolation to what the people did.

The answer is wonders. The passage says, "As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show My wonders." (Micah 7:15). It looks back to the days of coming out of Egypt, friends. And the word it lands on is wonders.

The answer is True. Verse 17 says, "They will come trembling from their strongholds in the presence of the LORD our God; they will tremble in fear of You." The dust-licking and the trembling are in the very same verse, friends. So the statement is true.

The answer is that He delights in loving devotion. God "…does not retain His anger forever, because He delights in loving devotion?" (Micah 7:18). The reason is right there in the verse, friends. The text points to who God is, not to anything people did.

The answer is into the depths of the sea. The message says, "You will cast out all our sins into the depths of the sea." (Micah 7:19). Depths is a deep word, friends, and it gives the picture of sins being put far down. I think that's a good place to leave them.

The answer is False. The message ends with God showing "…faithfulness to Jacob and loving devotion to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from the days of old." (Micah 7:20). The promise goes back to the days of old, friends. So it isn't something new.
